A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Real5-OmniDocBench and permit comparison of the complete text, equations, figures, tables and references. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 15 document-parsing systems on the constructed physical benchmark, including scenario scores and task-level results in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark results and reports additional evaluations. Table 1 contains 20 systems, with detailed results for selected systems in Tables 2–6.

M1.justification: The physical reconstruction procedure, annotation inheritance, quality audit and benchmark methodology remain unchanged. Newly evaluated model versions are comparison systems; no new parsing algorithm or model component is proposed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,355 OmniDocBench v1.5 originals and 6,775 physical variants across Scanning, Warping, Screen-Photography, Illumination and Skew. The document types, physical subconditions and parsing tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from 15 to 20 systems by adding Kimi K2.5, DeepSeek-OCR 2, MinerU2.5-Pro, GLM-OCR and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6. Tables 2–5 replace MinerU2.5 and PaddleOCR-VL-1.5 with MinerU2.5-Pro, GLM-OCR and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6; Table 6 also drops the original PaddleOCR-VL row. This substantially refreshes the evaluated comparison set.

E3.justification: The sample design, digital-baseline alignment protocol and NED, CDM, TEDS and overall scoring definitions are unchanged. No revised preprocessing, splits or execution settings are reported for retained comparisons.

E4.justification: Section 5.2 updates the evidence for its existing geometric and optical robustness questions: Tables 2–6 provide component-level diagnostics for newer specialists while removing older specialists' breakdowns. The analysis framework remains the same, with no new ablation, sensitivity study or failure-case analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental repeat counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The retained three-round manual audit concerns dataset quality control, not repeated experimental estimation.

E6.justification: All 15 original Table 1 result rows remain numerically unchanged, while five new result series and replacement diagnostic results substantially expand the evidence. The new leading entry is PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 at 93.19 overall; the previous leader, PaddleOCR-VL-1.5, retains 92.05. V2 contains unresolved MinerU2.5-Pro discrepancies: Screen-Photography is 92.29 in Table 1 versus 91.29 in Table 4, and Illumination is 91.42 versus 91.31 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The metric equations and mathematical definitions in Section 4 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The central claims about full-set physical reconstruction, factor-wise diagnosis, the reality gap and compact specialists outperforming larger generalists remain unchanged. The updated model-count statement and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 example support the existing empirical contribution without redefining its scientific claim.

C2.justification: The explanations involving geometric distortion, contextual cues, domain specialization and pipeline weaknesses are retained, with PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 replacing 1.5 as the featured example. No substantive new mechanism explanation, applicability boundary or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: V2 documents parameter counts for the added systems, including Kimi K2.5 at 1T, and adds a GLM-OCR model-hub source in reference 29. The benchmark dataset link, acquisition hardware, printing resolution and audit instructions remain unchanged; no additional execution hyperparameters or runtime details are supplied.

R1.justification: Five references are added for the newly evaluated systems, expanding the bibliography from 26 to 31 entries. Section 2 retains the same positioning relative to OmniDocBench, WildDoc, DocPTBench and other prior benchmarks.

P1.justification: V2 changes author order, slightly edits the affiliation and wording, and updates model mentions. It also duplicates the Physical Data Acquisition and Standardization heading as Sections 3.2 and 3.3, shifting Quality Audit to 3.4. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The same six figures and six tables remain. Table 1 gains rows, Tables 2–6 revise their row membership, and ranking emphasis and local page flow change. The illustrative figures and overall display organization are preserved.

improvement.justification: V2 broadens the empirical comparisons, but removes older specialists' detailed diagnostics and introduces reporting inconsistencies. MinerU2.5-Pro scores conflict between Table 1 and Tables 4–5; the introduction claims 17 models despite 20 listed entries; and Section 5.1 retains 91.25% Warping for PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 despite its table value of 92.48%. These reliability problems offset the usefulness of the expanded comparisons enough that a net quality improvement cannot be established confidently.
